Lesson 1.3 · 20 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

The regulatory map every BA must know

After this lesson you can:
  • Recognise the major directions and acts that shape each lifecycle stage
  • Use the India regulatory register as the working index
  • Know which regulator owns which obligation
On this page
  1. One journey, many rulebooks
  2. The register is the working index
  3. Who regulates what
  4. Where this lives in LoanOS
  5. Knowledge check

1. One journey, many rulebooks

No single document regulates a loan. A BA should be able to place the big ones on the lifecycle:

  • Digital Lending Directions, 2025 — conduct of digital lending end to end: LSP/DLA model, disclosures, cooling-off, fund flow.
  • KFS directions, 2024 — the standardised Key Facts Statement before contract execution.
  • KYC Master Direction, 2016 (as amended) — customer identification, due diligence, V-CIP, AML/CFT and FIU-IND reporting.
  • Fair lending / penal charges — penal charges as reasonable, disclosed charges; never capitalised, never penal interest.
  • Credit Information Reporting Directions, 2025 — fortnightly UCRF reporting to the CICs, correction clocks and compensation.
  • IRACP norms — income recognition, asset classification (SMA/NPA) and provisioning.
  • DPDP Act, 2023 and Rules, 2025 — personal-data consent, rights and breach duties (MeitY, not RBI).
  • IT and outsourcing directions, CERT-In directions — governance of the technology and vendors behind all of it.

2. The register is the working index

LoanOS maintains this map as a living artefact: the India regulatory register.

Every control family has a stable ID (for example RBI-KFS-2024, RBI-LSP-DLG), a why-it-matters summary and an implementation anchor pointing at the code or workflow that realises it.

This course cites those IDs throughout — when a lesson says a rule exists, the register row is where you verify the source, the date baseline and the platform anchor.

Treat the register the way engineers treat the architecture docs: if a lesson and the register disagree, the register wins, and the lesson must be fixed.

3. Who regulates what

A quick ownership table keeps escalations sane:

  • RBI — everything prudential and conduct-related for REs: lending directions, KFS, KYC, IRACP, outsourcing, IT governance, fraud, credit reporting.
  • MeitY / Data Protection Board — DPDP: personal-data consent, principal rights, breach notification.
  • CERT-In — cyber-incident reporting (6-hour clock) and log retention for Indian service providers, including LoanOS itself.
  • UIDAI — Aadhaar authentication rules and the prohibition on storing biometrics/OTP/PID.
  • CERSAI — central KYC records registry and security-interest registration.
  • FIU-IND — suspicious/cash transaction reporting under PMLA.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DL-2025 — The spine of digital lending conduct.
  • DPDP-2023 — Personal-data duties sit with MeitY's regime, parallel to RBI's.
  • CERT-IN-2022 — Cyber-incident and log-retention duties apply to the platform provider directly.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Document docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md — The control-family register this course cites — IDs, sources and implementation anchors.
  • Document docs/compliance/platform-admission-control-map.md — How control families gate platform admission.

Key terms

DLD 2025 KFS IRACP DPDP CERT-In UCRF

Knowledge check

1. A borrower demands erasure of their data mid-loan. Which regime governs the request itself?

  1. RBI Digital Lending Directions
  2. DPDP Act and Rules
  3. IRACP norms
  4. CERT-In directions
Show answer

B. Data-principal rights come from the DPDP regime — though statutory retention duties under RBI/PMLA rules can lawfully delay actual erasure.

2. Where in this repository do you verify that a regulatory claim in this course is current?

  1. The marketing site
  2. docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md
  3. Any RBI press release
  4. The test suite
Show answer

B. The register is the maintained control map with source URLs and a research baseline date; lessons cite its family IDs.
